security_audit.summary: All 50 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, Python template text, normal archive creation, and validation control flow. Two semantic issues remain: path traversal in the initializer and symlink-following during packaging can write or disclose files outside expected boundaries.

remediation.issue: The initializer accepts unvalidated skill names and permits paths outside the selected base directory.
remediation.suggestion: Validate skill names, reject path separators, and verify the resolved skill directory remains inside the resolved base before writing.

remediation.issue: The packager follows symlinks and can include files located outside the selected skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and verify every resolved file remains inside the skill root before adding it to the archive.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Allows Path Escape
semantic_findings.description: The initializer joins an unchecked skill name to the base path. Absolute names or traversal segments can create skill files outside the intended directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command-line value is used directly in a pathlib join without the documented name validation or a containment check, followed by directory and file writes.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink Targets Included in Skill Archive
semantic_findings.description: The packager recursively archives files without rejecting symlinks or checking resolved paths. A skill symlink can include local files outside the skill directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file and ZipFile.write follow file symlinks, while the loop performs no lstat or resolved-path containment check.

content.value_statement: Building reliable AI skills requires clear triggers, reusable resources, and validation. This skill guides planning, scaffolding, writing, packaging, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Guides selection of workflow, task, reference, or capability-based skill structures.
Scaffolds a skill directory with SKILL.md and sample resource files.
Validates frontmatter fields, naming rules, and description constraints.
Packages a validated skill folder into a distributable .skill archive.
Explains progressive disclosure and effective resource organization.
Provides workflow and output-format patterns for skill instructions.
limitations: Domain expertise and production resources must be supplied by the user.
Generated files are placeholders that require review, customization, or removal.
Validation checks basic metadata and structure, not script safety or behavioral quality.
Packaging does not exclude symlinks or sensitive files; review contents before creating an archive.

use_cases.title: Build a New Skill
use_cases.description: Plan the workflow, scaffold required files, and prepare a focused skill for validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: Apply consistent metadata, resource organization, instructions, and output patterns across a shared skill collection.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Refine triggers, reduce duplicated guidance, validate structure, and package a revised release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named [name] for [task]. Define clear triggers, a short workflow, and only the resources required.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a focused skill from a clear task description.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Clarify its trigger description, remove duplicated guidance, and organize detailed material through progressive disclosure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine an existing SKILL.md without changing its purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reusable Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable scripts, references, and assets for [skill]. Include only resources that reduce repeated work, then test added scripts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Extend a skill that needs deterministic helpers or domain references.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Advanced Skill Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Design or update [skill] for [complex workflow]. Add decision points, output requirements, validation steps, and package it after reviewing every included file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a complex skill for controlled distribution.

output_examples.input: Improve our large database support skill.
output: A shorter SKILL.md containing the core workflow and reference routing.
Separate references for provider-specific schemas and procedures.
Updated validation feedback with unresolved limitations.

output_examples.input: Create consistent output guidance for an incident report skill.
output_examples.output: A flexible report pattern covering summary, evidence, impact, response actions, and recommendations, with examples matched to the required detail.

best_practices: Use concrete user requests to define the skill purpose and trigger description.
Keep core instructions concise and move detailed variants into direct references.
Test every added script and remove unused placeholders before packaging.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague metadata that fails to explain when the skill should trigger.
Do not duplicate the same detailed guidance in SKILL.md and reference files.
Do not package unreviewed files, symlinks, secrets, or unnecessary resources.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides skill design and includes helpers for scaffolding, basic validation, and .skill archive packaging.

faq.question: Can it update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Skip initialization, review the existing files, refine the instructions and resources, then validate and package the result.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace package lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: The helper scripts require Python. The validator also requires the PyYAML package.

faq.question: Does validation inspect script security?
faq.answer: No. It checks basic frontmatter, naming, and description rules. Review and test executable resources separately.

faq.question: Which files should a skill include?
faq.answer: Every skill needs SKILL.md. Add scripts, references, and assets only when they directly support repeated work or required outputs.
